rationale: Used in 'they drew (them) into the ⲡⲱⲧⲏ of the city.' Could be from Coptic ⲡⲱⲧ 'race, course, road' or Greek πύλη 'gate.' Either fits the spatial sense of urban access-route.
Lyc compound ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲧⲏⲩ likely for ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' (with metathesis/dialectal vowel) or for ⲧⲏⲩ 'wind/breath/spirit.' Sense 'fear was in his heart' fits narrative context.
Lycopolitan abstract noun likely related to ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈ 'be many'; cf. accumulated tentative entry ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ. Used in 'because of the multitude of the herd of lions.'
Possessed feminine noun ⲧⲉⲙⲏⲣⲉ / ⲙⲏⲣⲉ 'herd, drove of cattle/animals.' Used for the lion-herd/pack in this kephalaion.
From ⲡⲱϩⲧ̄ 'pour, cast, leap.' In construction ⲣ̄ ⲡⲕⲉ ⲡⲱϩⲧ 'do also the leaping/casting' = 'they also leapt' (over the wall, into the city).
Possessed noun ⲡⲉⲥ- 'her' + ϩⲉⲉ (Lyc form of ϩⲏ 'face/aspect/manner'). In the storm-personification of the lion-cloak, 'wrath of her aspect.'
Coptic ⲱⲱⲥ 'crush, beat, pound.' Used here in causative ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲉⲱⲥ = ⲁ-ⲧⲣⲉⲩ-ⲱⲱⲥ 'to make them crush' = '(in order) to crush.'

Recurring noun denoting collectives — 'shall become how (great)' (line 17), 'crush hosts of thousands' (line 26). Etymology unclear, possibly from ⲧⲱⲱⲧ 'be united, joined.' Translation 'host(s)' fits both occurrences.
Plural noun modified by ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲏ 'of the beginning' — denotes pre-cosmogonic beings who scattered the primordial strife. Etymology obscure; possibly related to ϣⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'first' or to ⲱⲃϣ̄ in some sense.
Compound noun phrase: ⲡⲱⲧⲏ + ⲛ̄- + ⲡⲟⲗⲓⲥ. The narrative locus where lions burst into the city — likely the urban gate/main road.
Greek loanword κρηπίς 'foundation, base, raised platform.' The apostle stands upon this ⲕⲣⲏⲡⲓⲥ to address his disciples — likely an architectural feature of the city gate or wall.

Header construction ⲙ̄- + ⲧⲉⲁϩ. Sense unclear — possibly variant of standard Kephalaia ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁⲍ 'Of the Teacher,' or a section/chapter-specific title. The decorative brackets [> ·] [· <] confirm running-header function.
Already in glossary as 'support/foundation.' On this page (lines 14, 19) used of 'the support of the lions of Tigris' — the basis or strength of the lion population at Tigris.

Standard Manichaean technical term for Mani's own Living Gospel (or the Coptic-preserved Gospel of Mani). The apostle is here citing teaching 'out of the Great Gospel.' Direct attribution of cosmological narrative to this canonical text.
